Right printed page: only its left edge is visible, with a cropped running head and fragments of one text column.

main_text.p: fluctus super fluctus excitatus, qui in se-ipsum primùm insanierat,& sancta pro-triuerat,Spirituiq; gratię contumeliam intulerat; Ieroboam appositè dixeris,aut Israelitam Achab, aut Ægyptium illū Pha-raonem, aut Assyrium Nabucodonosor,vel hęc omnia contrahentes, unū & eundę nominabimus: quandoquidē eum om-nium vitia in se collegisse constat, dese-ctionem nempe Ieroboam, crudelitatem Achab, duritiem Pharaonis, sacrile-gium Nabucodonosoris, omnium deniq; in unum collectorum impjetatem] In myso-pog.{x}I-mò ipse, de seipso ; sinite me liberè, quod sentio, dicere. [Vna in re tantum iniuriam vobis fecit Constantius, quod me cum Cæsarem fecit, non vita priua-uit ?] quid vos iam Christiani cogitatis? quid molimini? Certè si vnquàm, sius-piàm, iuste in Tyrannum irruere possi-tis, hîc impiè statis ; Tyrannum Reli-gionis & suæ,& veræ non desertorem modò, sed irrisorem & oppressorem, immundis Spiritibus familiarem,perse-quutorem Sanctorum, in Saluatorem mundi blasphemum, Deo denique & hominibus odiosum. page.notes: Right printed page is cropped at the scan edge; its lines are only partly visible, so its fragments are copied as far as they can be seen and are doubtful. Italic words in the main text (Ieroboam, Achab, Pharaonis, Nabucodonosoris, Assyrium, Ægyptium, Pharaonem, Constantius, Cæsarem, Saluatorem) are read from the type style and may be off. The bracket after "impjetatem" and after "priua-uit ?" are printed as shown. The marginal note "In myso-pog." is read from a broken line; its s is written as s. The catchword "de-" is at the right below the last full line.
